summary.verdict: The raw material is at winner level: about 18 dated expert meetings, Before/After lists, second visits that report what changed, and a bioreactor story told as a chain of questions. The writing around it holds the page back: a generic opening, entries printed up to three times, change slots full of 'we learned' and 'consider', claims in the survey and Conclusion sections that go past the evidence, and several facts that disagree with the Entrepreneurship, Laws and Data Physicalization pages.
strengths: Bridge paragraphs between entries say what you still needed and why the next person, so meetings read as a chain. The Bioreactor and hardware pipeline is the best example.

Continuous engagement and the best Before/After lists name concrete changes: osmotic stress dropped, soil release abandoned, plate-to-soil model adopted, protectant tested on plants before going into the bacteria.
Honest reporting of problems: unintended stress in early plant results, low protein yield, membrane leakage on 4 September.
Outputs traced to people: the LINE platform to the Farmer Expo and Ms. Chen, the forum format to Green Media, the threat analysis to Mr. Chen.
A wide range of voices: smallholder and natural farmers, academics in Taiwan and at Stanford, two companies, an NGO, and the public.
priorities: Fix the facts that disagree with other pages: kill switch, target stresses, expansion countries, the printer-and-ink analogy, the target farmer, and which booth the 62-person survey covered.

Rewrite the abstract sheet and the opening around your own problem and your biggest changes. The lead sentence defines Human Practices, the bold "seven months, March to September" is wrong, and two Engagements lines miscount (five experts, three events). Cut the Human Practices definition in the body too.
Print each stakeholder entry once, and rewrite every change slot as an action (changed, dropped, added, chose) with dates and numbers.
Add a short context and prior-work paragraph and a limitations section, and answer the open questions on the page (the farmers' two questions, which stresses, kill switch or not).
Cut claims the data cannot carry: 'every stakeholder', 'fully tested', 'without ecological risks', 'confirm' for self-ratings, and 'increased' without a before-survey.

releaf: 3. Expert engagement (3.1 Pipelines in six tabs, 3.2 Continuous engagement)
4. Farmer engagement (4.1 Farmer interviews, 4.2 LINE platform)
5. Public engagement (5.1 Public forum, 5.2 Booth activities, 5.3 Plant stress event)
winners: Opening that states the team's own problem and HP stance
Stakeholder index: timeline cards, map or summary cards
Argued narrative where stakeholders cause design decisions, ordered by phase, design question or pivot
Outputs beyond the lab: guides, tools, education, community resources
Limitations or negative impacts, next steps, conclusion
skeleton.gap: ReLeaf has every part except limitations: the evolution map is the index, the pipeline bridges are the argued narrative, and LINE and the forum are outputs. The argued story is split across six tabs with entries repeated, so the decision chain is harder to follow than in NYU Abu Dhabi or WageningenUR, and the page ends on claims with no section on limits or harms.

extras: "sets off the green life" (three times): should be "sets off the green light".
"commercialization protectants" (in every CH Biotech copy): add "of", so it reads "commercialization of protectants".
"B. Subtilis powder or liquid" (three times): the species name takes a small s, "B. subtilis".

"Design a kill switch to prevent B. sub leakage and cause pollution" (twice): as written, the kill switch causes pollution. Write "Design a kill switch to stop B. subtilis leaking out and causing pollution".
"World. Veg": should be "the World Vegetable Center".
"can’t assess the resources": "assess" means judge. You mean "access" (reach), so write "cannot easily access the resources".
"B. subtilis. shifted toward designing": this sentence has no subject. Write "For the dry lab, we moved toward designing shorter or modified peptides...".
"“An on-site, on-demand bioreactor for smarter crop protection.": the slogan has no closing quotation mark. Add ” after "protection.".
"After the second meeting professor Chen": write "After the second meeting with Professor Chen", and end that paragraph with a full stop after "CH Biotech".
"including the speaker. farmers, and the general public": the full stop should be a comma, "the speaker, farmers and the general public".
"supporting local Taiwanese cocoa farming" under the heading "Coffee infographic": say coffee, cocoa or both, and make the heading match.

"six interactive stations, covering coffee farming, plant stress maps, drought sound recordings...": section 5.2 lists coffee, project introduction, data physicalization, ring toss, online game and crafts. Use the same six names in both places.
"March 27, 2026" (and every date in 3.2 Continuous engagement): the rest of the page writes "27 March". Use one date style on the whole wiki.
"Green Media (綠媒體), 5 September" on the map, but "meeting with Green Media in early July" in 5.1: give the date of the July meeting, or label the map card as the forum day.
"8/16 light cycle" (twice): say which number is hours of light, for example "16 h light, 8 h dark" or "8 h light, 16 h dark".
"B. subtilis might be intentionally released": check what Mr. Chen meant. If he meant by accident, write "accidentally released"; if he meant on purpose, say who might do it.
"DNA (>10k)" (three times): add the unit, for example "more than 10,000 ng" or "longer than 10 kb", so another team can repeat it.
"LEA14, NHP, and BoPep4": NHP appears only here and is never explained. Spell it out or remove it. The BIO Asia entry lists "ACCD, LEA14, and BoPep4", so make the two lists match.

notes.body: Farmers here asked you to add pests and disease. World Vegetable Center told you to stay with heat, and Dr. Sattely told you to pick one stress. The page never says which view won. Put the views side by side and say what you chose and why.
notes.excerpt_note: Both weigh one stakeholder against another by name and say what that meant for the plan.
notes.ballot: How well did it incorporate different stakeholder views?

notes.anchor: Ms. Chen is a natural farming practice farmer who believes we should not give additional support to crops
notes.title: Explain natural farming briefly
notes.body: International judges may not know what natural farming means in Taiwan. Add one line on what she does and does not use. The Entrepreneurship page calls her organic, so pick one term.
notes.after: Ms. Chen practises natural farming: she uses no [inputs] and gives plants little help, so they build their own resilience.

notes.anchor: Through the discussion, we learned that farmers might have concerns about the effectiveness of the technology solutions
notes.title: Split this long sentence
notes.body: This sentence runs about 55 words with four ideas in it. Short sentences make her point land, and it is one of the best points on the page.
notes.after: Ms. Chen worried that too much help makes plants weaker. A plant that is always protected may never build its own resilience. So we [set a dose limit of X / release protectant only when stress passes a threshold].
notes.excerpt_note: A farmer's complaint becomes a property the team can tune.

notes.anchor: Therefore, we designed a seed exchange platform that will allow us to track the owners of the seeds.
notes.title: Two descriptions of the seed platform
notes.body: Here the platform lets you 'track the owners of the seeds'. In section 4.2 it lets farmers post and match seed offers, and it was Ms. Chen's idea. Tracking owners and matching swaps are different tools. Use the 4.2 description here.

notes.anchor: In response, we incorporated this potential risk into the threat analysis of our business plan
notes.title: A risk, a response, a place
notes.body: Mr. Chen raised real-world risks (storms, animals, release), and you say exactly where they went: the threat analysis in your business plan. A link to that section would close the loop fully.
notes.excerpt_note: A critic's concerns become concrete obligations.
notes.ballot: How well did it incorporate different stakeholder views?

notes.anchor: During our interactions at the Farmer Expo and Ms. Chen’s interview, we realized that although there is information all across the internet
notes.title: The tool comes from what farmers said
notes.body: You trace the LINE platform back to two named conversations. That makes it an output of Human Practices, which is exactly what the ballot asks for.
notes.ballot: How inspiring an example is it to others?

notes.anchor: However, as our website is not intended to replace professional agricultural expertise
notes.title: You set a limit on your own tool
notes.body: Telling farmers to check official sources before acting is a responsible limit, and judges notice it. SDU-Denmark does the same when it says what its product must not claim.

notes.anchor: we incorporated a Google Form to collect suggestions and areas for improvement
notes.title: Report who has used the platform
notes.body: The section describes features but no users. How many people follow the account, and how many posts or form replies came in? Even small numbers show farmers used it.
notes.after: By [date], [number] people had added 農友助手 and [number] answered the feedback form. The most requested change was [x].
notes.ballot: How inspiring an example is it to others?

notes.anchor: we structured the forum to ensure that every participant’s voice could be heard
notes.title: The forum format came from advice
notes.body: You say what Green Media told you in July and how it shaped the forum. That makes the event itself a result of stakeholder input.

notes.anchor: including Prof. Chen, Dr. Li, and an expert from CH Biotech
notes.title: Introduce the forum speakers
notes.body: Dr. Li has no full name or role, and the page has three different Chens. Give each speaker a full name and a one-line role so judges can tell who said what.
notes.after: ...including Prof. [full name] ([role]), Dr. Li [full name] ([role]), and [name], a [role] at CH Biotech.

notes.anchor: Their insights helped us to further improve our design.
notes.title: Say how each expert changed the design
notes.body: This line promises design changes, but the three paragraphs below only report what each expert said. Add one 'what we changed' line to each, or remove the promise.
notes.after: Dr. Li: [what changed]. Prof. Chen: [what changed]. CH Biotech: [what changed].

notes.anchor: the goal should be to find a balance between growth and defense
notes.title: Your strongest theme deserves one paragraph
notes.body: Ms. Chen, Dr. Li, Prof. Chen and CH Biotech all warned against too much intervention. Four voices, from farmer to industry, saying one thing is your clearest social finding. Write one paragraph that links it to your design: dose limits, periodic release, seedling timing.
notes.ballot: How well did it incorporate different stakeholder views?

notes.anchor: The first concerned whether organic certification is required when using our bioreactor.
notes.title: Answer the farmers' two questions
notes.body: Farmers asked about organic certification and how many reactors a farm needs. The page records the questions but never the answers. Give your answer, even if it is 'we do not know yet, and here is how we will find out'.
notes.excerpt_note: An audience question leads to a clear decision on the page.
notes.ballot: How thoughtfully was it implemented? How well did they explain the context, rationale and prior work?

notes.anchor: and willingness to support local smallholder farmers and their agricultural products were all increased.
notes.title: No before-survey, so no 'increase'
notes.body: You only asked after the forum, so the data cannot show an increase. Also give how many people answered in each group (Fig. 1 seems to be one speaker). Report what you measured.
notes.after: After the forum, [n] members of the public answered. [x]% agreed that [statement]. We did not survey before the forum, so we cannot measure a change.
notes.excerpt_note: Heidelberg asks before and after, which is what lets it claim a change.

notes.anchor: For our ring toss booth, we wanted to help people understand the difference between biotic and abiotic stress
notes.title: A booth another team can copy
notes.body: You give the goal, the materials (labelled bottles, coloured rings) and the rule (match ring to stressor) in three sentences. A teacher could run this tomorrow.
notes.ballot: To what extent is the Human Practices work documented so that others can build upon it?

notes.anchor: Through this survey, we hope to capture a definitive reflection of our project’s ultimate impact
notes.title: Cut the survey promise
notes.body: This paragraph is mostly hopes ('definitive reflection', 'ultimate impact', 'more light to be shone'). The method fits in one sentence.
notes.after: After the booths, we gave visitors a KAP survey (62 responses).
notes.excerpt_note: Even winners slip here: Queen's calls 6,000 views 'genuine dialogue'.

notes.anchor: Our survey results from 62 respondents demonstrate that our interactive booth effectively communicated
notes.title: Which booth was surveyed?
notes.body: The Data Physicalization page says 62 of 116 visitors to its booth answered this survey. Here the same 62 stand for all six booths. Say which it was, and give the 116 if it applies.

notes.anchor: these metrics confirm that our hands-on games, interactive simulations, and station presentations successfully broke down
notes.title: Self-ratings do not confirm learning
notes.body: Visitors rated their own understanding, and nobody was tested. Write what the numbers are and drop 'confirm'. The same goes for the trust and 'active advocates' claims further down.
notes.after: Fewer than 5% of visitors rated their understanding as low.

notes.anchor: For the purpose of spreading more awareness about plant stress in our daily lives
notes.title: Give results or move this event
notes.body: This event has no date, no number of posts and no change. As it stands it reads like an announcement. Add what happened, or move it to the Education page.
notes.after: From [date] to [date], [number] people posted [number] photos of stressed plants on Instagram.

notes.anchor: every stakeholder’s insights directly impacted and led to changes in research direction
notes.title: Claim only what your entries show
notes.body: Several entries end with no change: Taiwan SMART Agriweek, the NCHU Symposium and Prof. Huang Tzu-Pi. 'Every' is easy to disprove.
notes.after: Across [number] conversations, stakeholder input changed our research direction, our plant model and our hardware.
notes.excerpt_note: Even winners slip here: Bielefeld's conclusion claims more than its own entries.

notes.anchor: We provided clear context for each stage of ReLeaf by examining existing agricultural methods, prior work
notes.title: Show the context you say you gave
notes.body: The ballot asks how well you explain context, rationale and prior work. This sentence claims it, but no section shows it: what protectants farmers use now, earlier iGEM teams with soil bacteria, Taiwan's GMO rules. Add a short context paragraph after the Overview, with sources.
notes.excerpt_note: Both explain the background a judge needs in plain words, with a source.
notes.ballot: How thoughtfully was it implemented? How well did they explain the context, rationale and prior work?

notes.anchor: ensuring our solution actively protects crops under climate stress without introducing ecological risks
notes.title: Limit the safety claim to what you tested
notes.body: Membrane leakage was still open on 4 September, and the kill switch question is not settled. 'Without introducing ecological risks' cannot be shown yet. SDU-Denmark limits its claim to exactly what was tested.
notes.after: ...we chose physical containment as our main safety layer. We are still testing the membrane for leaks.

notes.anchor: In previous pages, we have also mapped out our entire Human Practices journey on this page
notes.title: This sentence contradicts itself
notes.body: 'In previous pages' and 'on this page' cannot both be true, and the next sentence repeats the same idea. Keep one short sentence.
notes.after: This page maps every interaction and the step we took after it.

notes.anchor: By transparently detailing our successes, challenges, and methodology, we provide an accessible, step-by-step roadmap
notes.title: Give others something to download
notes.body: The ballot asks whether others can build on your work. Saying you made a roadmap is not enough. Offer the files: your interview question lists, the KAP survey forms, the stamp-card booth plan, and the LINE platform setup.
notes.excerpt_note: Each lists exactly what another team gets and how to reuse it.
notes.ballot: To what extent is the Human Practices work documented so that others can build upon it?

notes.anchor: Lastly, ReLeaf demonstrates how synthetic biology can move beyond abstract lab research
notes.title: Add limits before the big finish
notes.body: Both 2025 winners have a section on limitations or negative impacts. Yours could list membrane leakage, the open kill switch decision, no field trial yet, GMO approval, and natural farmers' worry about over-intervention. Put it before this paragraph.
notes.excerpt_note: NYU separates designed from proven; WageningenUR names a harm and a mitigation.
notes.ballot: How thoughtfully was it implemented? How well did they explain the context, rationale and prior work?
